text: In a game you win by making a straight line of three s on a 3 by 3 grid.
There are 8 winning lines of three s on a 3 by 3 grid.
Show each winning line of three s on the grids.
Three of the winning lines have been shown for you.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Another grid is 4 by 4.
You now need four s in a line to win.
Find the number of winning lines on a 4 by 4 grid.
You may use the grids to help you.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Another grid is 5 by 5.
You now need five s in a line to win.
Find the number of winning lines on a 5 by 5 grid.
You may use the grids to help you.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Another grid is 6 by 6.
You now need six s in a line to win.
Write down the number of winning lines on a 6 by 6 grid.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete this table using your answers to Question 1 and Question 2 and any patterns you notice.

Size of grid

3 by 3 8

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A grid is n by n.
You need n s in a line to win.
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the number of winning lines.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Jibreel draws a very large square grid.
He thinks there will be 583 winning lines of s on his grid.
Give a reason why he is wrong.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Harriet draws a square grid with 324 squares.
Find the number of winning lines of s on this grid.

4 A grid is n by n.
In a different game a winning line is one less than n.
To make a line, the s must be in squares that are next to each other.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
In a 3 by 3 grid you need two s in a line to win.
These diagrams show some of the diagonal winning lines.
Complete the table to find the number of winning lines with two s.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
In an n by n grid you need (n – 1) s in a line to win.
n must be at least 3.
In one grid the total number of winning lines is a square number less than 50.
Find the grid size.
